prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map shows a large open hall containing two parallel tiered wooden table structures extending away in front and to the left of the camera wearer from about 0.3 m at the bottom edge to roughly 3 m at their far ends, alongside background platforms at 4 to 6 m and columns on the right at 3 to 4 m. Across the five frames, the camera wearer's right arm (0.3 to 0.5 m away in the lower right) stays within arm's reach while gripping the near corner of the central wooden plank, whereas a second person starts on the right at about 2 to 2.5 m facing left in frames 1 and 2, retreats and moves leftward around the far end of the structure in frames 3 and 4 (reaching about 3 to 3.5 m away and became partly occluded behind the plank), and approaches the far end in frame 5 (~3 m away) facing toward the camera wearer with both hands within arm's reach of the board's far corners. The smooth brightness gradient along the long wooden surfaces makes their continuous 3D recession and relative height tiers much clearer than in the RGB image alone, where similar wood textures flatten the perspective. However, the depth map is unreliable around the second person's blurred head in frames 1 to 3—where the head merges into the depth of the vertical wooden beam behind them—and in frame 4 where the person's torso nearly vanishes into the dark background.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the foreground human figures and the central wooden plank against a black background, labeling the camera wearer's right forearm and a nearby floor lamp/cable in the lower right of frames 1 and 3 as 'person' (0.3 to 1 m away) and the second person in the upper right/center as 'person' (2 to 3.5 m away). It tracks the second person moving from the right side of the central table in frames 1 and 2 to behind its far end in frames 4 and 5, where their lower body is occluded by the ~2.5 m long wooden top so that only their upper torso and arms remain visible above the board. In frame 3, the map provides a clean boundary for the central wooden plank within the camera wearer's reach (0.3 to 3 m away), separating it from the adjacent wooden tier to the left and the lower bench to the right more distinctly than the similarly colored wood in the RGB strip. However, the map is highly unreliable across the sequence: it misclassifies the wooden plank as a 'surfboard' in frame 3 while failing to segment any wooden structures in frames 1, 2, 4, and 5, misses the camera wearer's arm entirely in frames 2, 4, and 5, merges the floor equipment with the wearer's arm mask in frame 1, and truncates the second person's head in frame 1.
descriptions.pose: The skeleton map renders 2D body keypoints in yellow and hand keypoints in magenta on a black background, capturing the spatial configuration of limbs only intermittently across the five frames. In frame 2, it accurately maps the second person standing about 2.5 m away to the right, facing and looking left with both arms raised in front of their torso, and in frame 5 it shows their shoulders and both arms reaching down to grip the far end of the wooden plank (~3 m from the camera wearer) while facing forward toward the camera wearer. In frame 3, a magenta hand skeleton at the bottom right (~0.4 m away) captures the exact finger curl of the camera wearer's right hand gripping the near edge of the board within immediate reach, a fine articulation that is harder to see in the dark lower corner of the RGB frame. Conversely, the pose map is severely unreliable elsewhere: it completely misses the second person in frames 3 and 4 as they walk around the far end of the table, misses the camera wearer's hand in frames 1, 2, 4, and 5, and hallucinates horizontally sideways body skeletons in frames 1 and 5 along the outstretched arms and table edge while failing to detect any facial orientation toward the camera wearer due to face blurring.
